notes: Perfect claim overlap (C32, C33, C34, C35, C50) regarding ramped figure experiments. Both express uncertainty: LLM wants 'matched parametric manipulations' for spectral vs. temporal susceptibility claims; peer reviewers want to 'see what the model predicts for the ramped SFG.'

High overlap (C6, C53, C54, C60, C98) on temporal coherence model claims. Both uncertain about model validation: LLM criticizes lack of 'quantitative model fitting, goodness-of-fit metrics'; peer reviewers are 'disappointed by the integration between data and modeling' and want 'model simulations for all experimental manipulations.'

Strong overlap (C5, C95, C96) on inadequacy of adaptation-based models. LLM finds claims UNSUPPORTED due to lack of 'formal model simulations or quantitative predictions.' Peer reviewers SUPPORT by accepting temporal coherence as 'most appropriate model,' implicitly endorsing that adaptation models are insufficient. Disagreement reflects different evidentiary standards.

Moderate overlap (C2, C26, C27, C28, C46) on Experiment 1 figure detection findings. Both SUPPORT the core psychoacoustic results. Peer review covers broader claim set including multiple experiments, but shared claims show clear agreement on robust detection with appropriate controls.

Overlap on C44, C45 regarding cortical mechanisms and integration windows. LLM is UNCERTAIN, calling neural mechanism inference 'reasonable but speculative' and wanting 'direct temporal integration measurements.' Peer reviewers SUPPORT, affirming findings are 'beyond segregation capacities of core auditory cortex' and accepting cortical involvement claims.

Overlap on C30, C31 regarding Experiment 3 temporal scaling. Both SUPPORT the finding that performance depends on number of chords rather than absolute duration. Peer review groups these with broader experimental findings, all affirmed as appropriately performed.

Overlap on C36, C37 regarding Experiment 5 showing background context is unnecessary. Both SUPPORT this finding. LLM notes appropriate null result interpretation; peer reviewers affirm studies were 'appropriately performed with adequate controls.'
Overlap on C38, C39 regarding Experiment 6a showing robustness to 50ms noise interruptions. Both SUPPORT this finding. Peer reviewers describe segregation despite noise interruptions as 'remarkable.'

Overlap on C40, C41, C42 regarding Experiment 6b with 500ms interruptions. LLM is UNCERTAIN due to 'modest effect size' and extrapolation concerns about '3s integration windows.' Peer reviewers SUPPORT, describing segregation with interruptions up to 500ms as 'remarkable' and affirming appropriate experimental performance.

Minimal overlap (C7 only) on temporal coherence as organizational principle. Both UNCERTAIN: LLM wants 'additional validation through neural recordings, causal manipulations'; peer reviewers find framework 'promising' but want 'more comprehensive model-data comparison.'

LLM evaluates C48 (AXB experiment, Experiment 2) regarding figure-specific detection vs. local features. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this claim. LLM uncertain about whether holistic object representations are demonstrated.

Peer review evaluates C4 (automatic segregation mechanisms) not specifically addressed in LLM results. Peer reviewers support interpretation about underlying mechanisms and cortical involvement. LLM R7 touches on related cortical claims (C44, C45) but C4 itself not directly evaluated.
